locator.section: 8.2 (top of p.151): reverse-second-step of Eq. 8.19; homolytic H-transfer from carbon to a heteroatom radical cation forming the distonic radical ion .R'Y+H

evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.19 is a GENERIC scheme, R'-H + Y+. <=> (R'....H....Y)+. <=> R'. + H-Y+ : a homolytic hydrogen-atom transfer from a carbon to a heteroatom radical-cation site, yielding a distonic radical ion (text: 'hydrogen-transfer rearrangements from carbon atoms to O, Cl, or CN to yield the distonic radical ion .R'Y+H'). ARC COUNT (convention D): the page draws 0 electron-pushing arcs -- it conveys the mechanism only by the dotted-bond transition state (R'....H....Y)+. and the word 'homolytic' printed over both equilibrium arrows; the horizontal underbrackets are species-grouping brackets (the unshown remainder of the ion joining R' to Y), NOT curved arrows. Book draws 0 arc(s); all three moves are implicit homolysis/H-transfer hooks required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). INSTANTIATION (convention F -- generic scheme, the page prints no m/z and no %): realized as the gamma-H transfer of the n-ionized pentan-2-one molecular ion, Y = carbonyl O6 with charge AND odd electron localized as =[O+.] per convention B; a six-membered TS moves the gamma-H (H8, written [1H] so RDKit keeps it as a mapped node) from C5 to O6. This is the McLafferty first step and belongs to exactly the family discussed at the foot of this same page (2-hexanone gamma-H/beta-cleavage, Eqs 4.33/8.2). Three fishhooks (homolytic H-atom transfer): move<1> O6 odd electron into the forming O6-H8 bond; move<2> one C5-H8 bonding electron into that same O-H bond (so the new O-H bond receives its 2 electrons); move<3> the other C5-H8 electron back onto C5, the new gamma-carbon radical. The product is a distonic radical cation that is an ISOMER of M+. (same formula C5H10O, m/z 86.0726, no fragment lost); its m/z is curator-computed from this instantiation, not printed in the book. The page shows equilibrium arrows, so the step is marked reversible.

No MØD rule is indexed to equation 8.19 (rule_index by_equation has no '8.19' key; the ch.8 index runs 8.1-8.14). The IDENTICAL elementary transformation -- homolytic gamma C-H -> carbonyl-O radical cation giving a C-radical plus a protonated-carbonyl distonic ion -- is encoded by the rH-family rule IMS_8_2_bidirectional_down (indexed to Eq. 8.2). VERIFIED (convention E) against its DFS: '[C]14{=}[O+.]19' with a gamma '[C]5([H]7)' >> '[C.]5' + '{=}[O+]19([H]7)'. It cleaves the gamma C-H, forms the O-H, relocates the odd electron onto the gamma carbon, and converts =O+. into =O+(H) -- exactly move<1..3> of this record. The cleaved C-H is incident (via the migrating H) to the O that forms the new O-H bond: correct geometry, no mismatch. The only difference is chain length (the rule uses a 2-hexanone-length backbone; this record instantiates 2-pentanone, one CH2 shorter). Equation 8.19's forward/reverse equilibrium maps directly onto the IMS_8_2_bidirectional_down / IMS_8_2_bidirectional_up pair.
